name: Yogurt (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Yogurt [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 171284 (Yogurt, plain, whole milk), macros, minerals, vitamins, full amino-acid and fatty-acid panel, cholesterol
Marshall/Cheng et al., Determination of Sugars in Yogurt by HPLC, J Dairy Sci 1987 70, doi:10.3168/jds.S0022-0302(87)80124-8, residual lactose/galactose/glucose
Fernandez-Garcia E & McGregor JU 1994, Determination of organic acids during fermentation and cold storage of yogurt, J Dairy Sci 77:2934-2939, PMID 7836580, lactic/citric/acetic/orotic acids
Fermented-milk galactose review, Int Dairy J / Food Chem, doi:10.1016/j.idairyj.2017.06.001 (total galactose 2.3-2.4 g/100g)
FooDB FOOD00620 (Yogurt), base record; noise flagged for removal
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources for microbial growth on plain yogurt are lactic acid (~0.9 g/100g), lactose (~3.7 g/100g) and free galactose (~1.0 g/100g); glucose stays at trace because starter bacteria consume it while galactose accumulates. Organic acids (lactic + citric) were completely missing from the FooDB profile and are the key correction. Removed a large block of soy isoflavones/plant lignans plus methylxanthines that are FooDB matrix contamination for plain dairy yogurt; cholesterol an
curation_added: L-lactic acid (0.9 g/100g, dominant organic acid, was entirely absent)
specific sugars with real amounts: lactose 3.7, D-galactose 1.0, D-glucose trace
L-phenylalanine and L-valine (missing from FooDB amino-acid list)
quantitative minerals and vitamins from USDA FDC 171284

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
